:question/problem:
Find the derivative of $\mathbf f(t) + 2\mathbf g(t)$ with respect to $t,$ where $\mathbf f(t)$ and $\mathbf g(t)$ are defined as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf{f}(t) & =(4{t}^{2}+9)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}-\left(\frac{1}{t-2}\right)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+\operatorname{cos}2t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k} \\ \mathbf{g}(t) & =(4t-1)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+{e}^{3t}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+\operatorname{cos}2t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k}\end{aligned}
$$
:question/worked-solution:
Using the constant multiple rule and the sum rule, we have

$$
(\mathbf f(t) + 2\mathbf g(t))' = \mathbf f'(t) + 2\mathbf g'(t).
$$

Now, let's find the derivative of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{t}^{2}+9)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}\left(-\frac{1}{t-2}\right)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}2t)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k} \\  & =8t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+\frac{1}{(t-2)^{2}}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}-2\operatorname{sin}2t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k}, \\ {\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t-1)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{3t})\mathbf{j}+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}2t)\mathbf{k} \\  & =4\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+3{e}^{3t}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}-2\operatorname{sin}2t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf{f}(t)+2\mathbf{g}(t))^{'} & ={\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t)+2{\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t) \\  & =(8t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+\frac{1}{(t-2)^{2}}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}-2\operatorname{sin}2t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k})+2(4\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+3{e}^{3t}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}-2\operatorname{sin}2t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k}) \\  & =8(t+1)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+(\frac{1}{(t-2)^{2}}+6{e}^{3t})\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}-6\operatorname{sin}2t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k}.\end{aligned}
$$

:question/problem: Find $\big( u(t) \mathbf g(t) \big)'$ where $\mathbf g (t) = {\left[ \begin{array}{c}\ln   t \\ - t \\ {e}^{2 t}\end{array} \right]}$ and $u(t) = t.$
:question/worked-solution:
Using the scalar function multiple rule, we have

$$
\big( u(t) \mathbf g(t) \big)' = u'(t) \mathbf{g}(t) + u(t) \mathbf{g}'(t).
$$

Let's find $\mathbf g'(t)$ and $u'(t),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t) & =\begin{bmatrix}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}t) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-t) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}{e}^{2t}\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}\frac{1}{t} \\ -1 \\ 2{e}^{2t}\end{bmatrix} \\ {u}^{'}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(u(t)\mathbf{g}(t))^{'} & ={u}^{'}(t)\mathbf{g}(t)+u(t){\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t) \\  & =1\cdot \begin{bmatrix}\operatorname{ln}t \\ -t \\ {e}^{2t}\end{bmatrix}+t\cdot \begin{bmatrix}\frac{1}{t} \\ -1 \\ 2{e}^{2t}\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}\operatorname{ln}t \\ -t \\ {e}^{2t}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -t \\ 2t{e}^{2t}\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}1+\operatorname{ln}t \\ -2t \\ (2t+1){e}^{2t}\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

:question/problem: Find $(\mathbf f \circ u)'(t),$ if $\mathbf f(u) = \ln u \, \mathbf i + (u^2+5) \, \mathbf j + 4u \, \mathbf k$ and $u(t) =2t^3.$
:question/worked-solution:
By the chain rule, we have 

$$
(\mathbf f \circ u)'(t) = \mathbf{f}'(u(t)) u'(t).
$$

Now, let's find the derivative of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\mathbf{f}}^{'}(u) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}(\operatorname{ln}u)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}({u}^{2}+5)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}(4u)\mathbf{k} \\  & =\frac{1}{u}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+2u\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+4\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k}, \\ {u}^{'}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3})=6{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf{f}∘u)^{'}(t) & ={\mathbf{f}}^{'}(u(t)){u}^{'}(t) \\  & =(\frac{1}{u(t)}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+2u(t)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+4\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k}){u}^{'}(t) \\  & =(\frac{1}{2{t}^{3}}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+2(2{t}^{3})\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+4\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k})\cdot 6{t}^{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{t}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+24{t}^{5}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+24{t}^{2}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k}.\end{aligned}
$$

:question/problem:
Find $\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt} (\mathbf f \cdot \mathbf g)(t),$ given the following functions $\mathbf f(t)$ and $\mathbf g(t)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf{f}(t) & =\sqrt{t}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+{t}^{2}\mathbf{j} \\ \mathbf{g}(t) & =\frac{1}{t}\mathbf{i}+{e}^{t}\mathbf{j}\end{aligned}
$$
:question/worked-solution:
Using the dot product rule, we have

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(\mathbf{f} \cdot \mathbf{g})(t) = \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(\mathbf{f}(t)) \cdot \mathbf{g}(t) + \mathbf{f}(t) \cdot \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(\mathbf{g}(t))
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}\mathbf{f}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{t})\mathbf{i}+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\mathbf{j} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+2t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}, \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}\mathbf{g}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}\left(\frac{1}{t}\right)\mathbf{i}+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t})\mathbf{j} \\  & =-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+{e}^{t}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt} (\mathbf f \cdot \mathbf g)(t)
&= \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(\mathbf{f}(t)) \cdot \mathbf{g}(t) + \mathbf{f}(t) \cdot \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(\mathbf{g}(t)) \\[3pt]
&= \left(\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{t}} \,\mathbf i +2t \, \mathbf j \right) \cdot \left(\dfrac{1}{t} \,  \mathbf i + e^t \,  \mathbf j \right) +
\left(\sqrt{t} \,  \mathbf i + t^2 \,  \mathbf j \right) \cdot \left(-\dfrac{1}{t^2}  \, \mathbf i + e^t \, \mathbf j  \right) \\[3pt]		 
&=\dfrac{1}{2t\sqrt{t}}  +2te^t    +  \left(-\dfrac{\sqrt{t}}{t^2}\right)    + t^2e^t \\[3pt]
&=\dfrac{\sqrt{t}}{2t^2}  -  \dfrac{\sqrt{t}}{t^2} +2te^t   + t^2e^t  \\[3pt]
&= -\dfrac{\sqrt{t}}{2t^2} +\left(2t+t^2\right)e^t.
\end{aligned}
$$

:question/problem: Find $(u(t)\mathbf{f}(t))^{'}$ where $\mathbf{f}(t)=\begin{bmatrix}\operatorname{sin}t \\ 2t-8 \\ {5}^{t}\end{bmatrix}$ and $u(t)={t}^{2}.$
:question/worked-solution:
Using the scalar function multiple rule, we can write

$$
(u(t)\mathbf{f}(t))^{'}={u}^{'}(t)\mathbf{f}(t)+u(t){\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t)
$$

Let's find ${u}^{′}(t)$ and ${\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t).$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t) & =\begin{bmatrix}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}t) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t-8) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({5}^{t})\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}\operatorname{cos}t \\ 2 \\ {5}^{t}\operatorname{ln}5\end{bmatrix} \\ {u}^{'}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})=2t\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(u(t)\mathbf{f}(t))^{'} & ={u}^{'}(t)\mathbf{f}(t)+u(t){\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t) \\  & ={t}^{2}\begin{bmatrix}\operatorname{cos}t \\ 2 \\ {5}^{t}\operatorname{ln}5\end{bmatrix}+2t\begin{bmatrix}\operatorname{sin}t \\ 2t-8 \\ {5}^{t}\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}{t}^{2}\operatorname{cos}t \\ 2{t}^{2} \\ {5}^{t}{t}^{2}\operatorname{ln}5\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2t\operatorname{sin}t \\ 4{t}^{2}-16t \\ {5}^{t}\cdot 2t\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}{t}^{2}\operatorname{cos}t+2t\operatorname{sin}t \\ 6{t}^{2}-16t \\ {5}^{t}{t}^{2}\operatorname{ln}5+{5}^{t}\cdot 2t\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

:question/problem:
Find $(\mathbf{f}\cdot \mathbf{g})^{'}(t)$, given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf{f}(t) & =20t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}-2t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+(2+5t)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k} \\ \mathbf{g}(t) & ={t}^{3}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+({t}^{2}+t)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k}\end{aligned}
$$
:question/worked-solution:
Using the dot product rule, we can write:

$$
(\mathbf{f}\cdot \mathbf{g})^{'}(t)={\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t)\cdot \mathbf{g}(t)+\mathbf{f}(t)\cdot {\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t)
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(20t)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2+5t)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k} \\  & =20\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}-2\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+5\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k} \\ {\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3})\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}+t)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k} \\  & =3{t}^{2}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}+(2t+1)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf{f}\cdot \mathbf{g})^{'}(t) & ={\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t)\cdot \mathbf{g}(t)+\mathbf{f}(t)\cdot {\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t) \\  & =(20\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}-2\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+5\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k})\cdot ({t}^{3}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+({t}^{2}+t)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k})+(20t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}-2t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+(2+5t)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k})\cdot (3{t}^{2}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}+(2t+1)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k}) \\  & =(20{t}^{3}-2t+5({t}^{2}+t))+(60{t}^{3}-2t+(2+5t)(2t+1)) \\  & =80{t}^{3}+15{t}^{2}+10t+2\end{aligned}
$$

:question/problem:
Find $(\mathbf{f}\times \mathbf{g})^{'}(t)$ where

$$
\mathbf{f}(t)=\begin{bmatrix}3{t}^{2} \\ t+4 \\ 8\end{bmatrix},\hspace{2em}\mathbf{g}(t)=\begin{bmatrix}t+2 \\ -2{t}^{2} \\ 5t\end{bmatrix}
$$
:question/worked-solution:
Using the cross product rule, we can write:

$$
(\mathbf{f}\times \mathbf{g})^{'}(t)={\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t)\times \mathbf{g}(t)+\mathbf{f}(t)\times {\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t)
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t) & =\begin{bmatrix}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t+4) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(8)\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}6t \\ 1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\ {\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t) & =\begin{bmatrix}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t+2) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-2{t}^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5t)\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -4t \\ 5\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t)\times \mathbf{g}(t) & =\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ 6t & 1 & 0 \\ t+2 & -2{t}^{2} & 5t\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 \\ -2{t}^{2} & 5t\end{vmatrix}\mathbf{i}-\begin{vmatrix}6t & 0 \\ t+2 & 5t\end{vmatrix}\mathbf{j}+\begin{vmatrix}6t & 1 \\ t+2 & -2{t}^{2}\end{vmatrix}\mathbf{k} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}5t \\ -30{t}^{2} \\ -12{t}^{3}-t-2\end{bmatrix} \\ \mathbf{f}(t)\times {\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t) & =\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ 3{t}^{2} & t+4 & 8 \\ 1 & -4t & 5\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}t+4 & 8 \\ -4t & 5\end{vmatrix}\mathbf{i}-\begin{vmatrix}3{t}^{2} & 8 \\ 1 & 5\end{vmatrix}\mathbf{j}+\begin{vmatrix}3{t}^{2} & t+4 \\ 1 & -4t\end{vmatrix}\mathbf{k} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}37t+20 \\ 8-15{t}^{2} \\ -12{t}^{3}-t-4\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf{f}\times \mathbf{g})^{'}(t) & =\begin{bmatrix}5t \\ -30{t}^{2} \\ -12{t}^{3}-t-2\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}37t+20 \\ 8-15{t}^{2} \\ -12{t}^{3}-t-4\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}42t+20 \\ 8-45{t}^{2} \\ -24{t}^{3}-2t-6\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

:question/problem: If $\mathbf{f}(u)=\begin{bmatrix}2u \\ {u}^{2} \\ 3\end{bmatrix}$ and $u(t)=2t+2$, then $(\mathbf{f}∘u)^{'}(t)=$
:question/worked-solution:
Using the chain rule, we can write

$$
(\mathbf{f}∘u)^{'}(t)={\mathbf{f}}^{'}(u(t)){u}^{'}(t)
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{\mathbf{f}}^{'}(u) & =\begin{bmatrix}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}(2u) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}\hspace{0.167em}({u}^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}(3)\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 2u \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\ {u}^{'}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t+2)=2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf{f}∘u)^{'}(t) & =\mathbf{f}'(u(t))u'(t) \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 2u(t) \\ 0\end{bmatrix}\cdot {u}^{'}(t) \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 2(2t+2) \\ 0\end{bmatrix}\cdot 2 \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 8t+8 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

:question/problem: Find $(u(t)\mathbf{g}(t))^{'}$ where $\mathbf{g}(t)=⟨3{t}^{2},\hspace{0.222em}3-t,\hspace{0.222em}3t⟩$ and $u(t) = t^{3}$.
:question/worked-solution: Differentiate each component of the scalar product. First $u(t)g(t)=\langle3t^5,3t^3-t^4,3t^4\rangle$. Therefore $$(ug)'(t)=\langle15t^4,9t^2-4t^3,12t^3\rangle.$$

:question/problem: If $\mathbf{f}(t)=\operatorname{cos}u\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+(1-{u}^{2})\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+12\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k}$ and $u(t)={t}^{3}$ then $(\mathbf{f}∘u)^{'}(t)=$
:question/worked-solution:
Using the chain rule, we can write

$$
(\mathbf{f}∘u)^{'}(t)={\mathbf{f}}^{'}(u(t)){u}^{'}(t)
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{\mathbf{f}}^{'}(u) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}(\operatorname{cos}u)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}(1-{u}^{2})\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}(12)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k} \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}u\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}-2u\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+0\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k} \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}u\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}-2u\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j} \\ {u}^{'}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3})=3{t}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf{f}∘u)^{'}(t) & ={\mathbf{f}}^{'}(u(t))\cdot {u}^{'}(t) \\  & =(-\operatorname{sin}(u(t))\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}-2(u(t))\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j})\cdot {u}^{'}(t) \\  & =(-\operatorname{sin}({t}^{3})\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}-2({t}^{3})\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j})\cdot 3{t}^{2} \\  & =-3{t}^{2}\operatorname{sin}{t}^{3}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}-6{t}^{5}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}\end{aligned}
$$

:question/problem:
Differentiate $\mathbf{f}(t)+\mathbf{g}(t)$ with respect to $t$, given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf{f}(t) & =⟨3t-1,\hspace{0.222em}6-t,\hspace{0.222em}7t⟩ \\ \mathbf{g}(t) & =⟨{t}^{2},\hspace{0.222em}1-{t}^{2},\hspace{0.222em}t⟩\end{aligned}
$$
:question/worked-solution:
By the sum rule, we have

$$
(\mathbf{f}(t)+\mathbf{g}(t))^{'}={\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t)+{\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t)
$$

Let's find the derivatives of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3t-1),\hspace{0.222em}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6-t),\hspace{0.222em}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(7t)⟩ \\  & =⟨3,\hspace{0.222em}-1,\hspace{0.222em}7⟩ \\ {\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\hspace{0.222em}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-{t}^{2}),\hspace{0.222em}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2t,\hspace{0.222em}-2t,\hspace{0.222em}1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf{f}(t)+\mathbf{g}(t))^{'} & ={\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t)+{\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t) \\  & =⟨3,\hspace{0.222em}-1,\hspace{0.222em}7⟩+⟨2t,\hspace{0.222em}-2t,\hspace{0.222em}1⟩ \\  & =⟨2t+3,\hspace{0.222em}-2t-1,\hspace{0.222em}8⟩\end{aligned}
$$

:question/problem:
Find the value of $(3\mathbf{h}(t)-2\mathbf{g}(t))^{'}$ at $t = 2$, if
$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf{h}(t) & =⟨2{t}^{2},\hspace{0.222em}t-3,\hspace{0.222em}8+{t}^{3}⟩ \\ \mathbf{g}(t) & =⟨{t}^{2}+2t,\hspace{0.222em}8,\hspace{0.222em}2{t}^{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$
:question/worked-solution: Differentiate componentwise: $h'(t)=\langle4t,1,3t^2\rangle$ and $g'(t)=\langle2t+2,0,6t^2\rangle$. Thus $$(3h-2g)'(2)=3\langle8,1,12\rangle-2\langle6,0,24\rangle=\langle12,3,-12\rangle.$$

:question/problem:
Find the value of $(\mathbf{f}(t)-3\mathbf{g}(t))^{'}$ at $t=0,$ if 

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf{f}(t) & =⟨2\sqrt{t+1},\hspace{0.167em}{t}^{3},\hspace{0.167em}\operatorname{ln}(t+1)⟩, \\ \mathbf{g}(t) & =⟨\frac{1}{3(t+1)},\hspace{0.167em}\operatorname{sin}t,\hspace{0.167em}\operatorname{tan}t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
:question/worked-solution:
First, notice that

$$
(\mathbf{f}(t)-3\mathbf{g}(t))^{'}={\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t)-3{\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t).
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\sqrt{t+1}),\hspace{0.167em}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}),\hspace{0.167em}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}(t+1))⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{\sqrt{t+1}},\hspace{0.167em}3{t}^{2},\hspace{0.167em}\frac{1}{t+1}⟩ \\ {\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}\left(\frac{1}{3(t+1)}\right),\hspace{0.167em}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}t),\hspace{0.167em}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{tan}t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{3(t+1)^{2}},\hspace{0.167em}\operatorname{cos}t,\hspace{0.167em}{\operatorname{sec}}^{2}t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf{f}(0)-3\mathbf{g}(0))^{'} & ={\mathbf{f}}^{'}(0)-3{\mathbf{g}}^{'}(0) \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{\sqrt{0+1}},\hspace{0.167em}3(0)^{2},\hspace{0.167em}\frac{1}{0+1}⟩-3⟨-\frac{1}{3(0+1)^{2}},\hspace{0.167em}\operatorname{cos}0,\hspace{0.167em}{\operatorname{sec}}^{2}0⟩ \\  & =⟨1,0,1⟩-3⟨-\frac{1}{3},1,1⟩ \\  & =⟨1,0,1⟩-⟨-1,3,3⟩ \\  & =⟨2,-3,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

:question/problem:
Find the value of $(2\mathbf{f}(t)-\mathbf{g}(t))^{'}$ at $t=-1,$ if 

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf{f}(t) & =⟨8\sqrt{3-t},\hspace{0.167em}\operatorname{sin}(\pi t),\hspace{0.167em}\operatorname{ln}(2t)⟩, \\ \mathbf{g}(t) & =⟨{t}^{2}-t,\hspace{0.167em}\pi {t}^{2},\hspace{0.167em}1-{t}^{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
:question/worked-solution:
First, notice that

$$
(2\mathbf{f}(t)-\mathbf{g}(t))^{'}=2{\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t)-{\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t).
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(8\sqrt{3-t}),\hspace{0.167em}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}(\pi t)),\hspace{0.167em}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}(2t))⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{4}{\sqrt{3-t}},\hspace{0.167em}\pi \operatorname{cos}(\pi t),\hspace{0.167em}\frac{1}{t}⟩ \\ {\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-t),\hspace{0.167em}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\pi {t}^{2}),\hspace{0.167em}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨2t-1,\hspace{0.167em}2\pi t,\hspace{0.167em}-2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

:question/problem:

$$
(\mathbf{2}f(t)+5\mathbf{g}(t))^{'}=2{\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t)+5{\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t).

$$

$$

Hence , we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(2\mathbf{f}(1)+5\mathbf{g}(1))^{'} & =2{\mathbf{f}}^{'}(1)+5{\mathbf{g}}^{'}(1) \\  & =2\begin{bmatrix}\frac{1}{\sqrt{3+1}} \\ -\operatorname{sin}(1-1) \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+5\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 2(1) \\ 2(1+1)\end{bmatrix} \\  & =2\begin{bmatrix}\frac{1}{2} \\ 0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+5\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}10 \\ 10 \\ 20\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}11 \\ 10 \\ 20\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}

$$

$$

Using the sum rule, we can write

$$
(\mathbf{f}(t)+\mathbf{g}(t)+\mathbf{h}(t))^{'}={\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t)+{\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t)+{\mathbf{h}}^{'}(t)
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$

:question/problem: Given $\mathbf{f}(t)=2{t}^{3}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}-2t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+(1+5{t}^{2})\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k}$, find $({\mathbf{f}}^{'}\cdot \mathbf{f})^{'}(t).$
:question/worked-solution:
Using the dot product rule, we can write:

$$({\mathbf{f}}^{'}\cdot \mathbf{f})^{'}(t)={\mathbf{f}}^{''}(t)\cdot \mathbf{f}(t)+{\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t)\cdot {\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t)$$

Let's now find the first and second derivative of the function.

$$\begin{aligned}{\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3})\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1+5{t}^{2})\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k} \\  & =2\cdot 3{t}^{2}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}-2\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+5\cdot 2t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k} \\  & =6{t}^{2}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}-2\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+10t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k} \\ {\mathbf{f}}^{''}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6{t}^{2})\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(10t)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k} \\  & =6\cdot 2t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+(0)\mathbf{j}+(10)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k} \\  & =12t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+10\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k}\end{aligned}$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$\begin{aligned}({\mathbf{f}}^{'}\cdot \mathbf{f})^{'}(t) & ={\mathbf{f}}^{''}(t)\cdot \mathbf{f}(t)+{\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t)\cdot {\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t) \\  & =(12t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+10\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k})\cdot (2{t}^{3}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}-2t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+(1+5{t}^{2})\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k})+(6{t}^{2}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}-2\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+10t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k})\cdot (6{t}^{2}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}-2\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+10t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k}) \\  & =(12t\cdot 2{t}^{3}+0\cdot (-2t)+10\cdot (1+5{t}^{2}))+((6{t}^{2})^{2}+(-2)^{2}+(10t)^{2}) \\  & =24{t}^{4}+0+10+50{t}^{2}+36{t}^{4}+4+100{t}^{2} \\  & =60{t}^{4}+150{t}^{2}+14\end{aligned}$$

:question/problem: Given $\mathbf{f}(t)=({t}^{3}-1)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+({t}^{2}-2)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+4{t}^{2}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k}$, evaluate $({\mathbf{f}}^{'}\cdot \mathbf{f})^{'}(0).$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$\begin{aligned}({\mathbf{f}}^{'}\cdot \mathbf{f})^{'}(0) & ={\mathbf{f}}^{''}(0)\cdot \mathbf{f}(0)+{\mathbf{f}}^{'}(0)\cdot {\mathbf{f}}^{'}(0) \\  & =(6(0)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+2\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+8\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k})\cdot (({0}^{3}-1)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+({0}^{2}-2)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+4(0)^{2}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k})+(3(0)^{2}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+2(0)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+8(0)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k})\cdot (3(0)^{2}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+2(0)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+8(0)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k}) \\  & =(2\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+8\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k})\cdot (-\mathbf{i}-2\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}) \\  & =0(-1)+2(-2)+(0) \\  & =-4\end{aligned}$$

:question/problem: If $\mathbf{g}(u)=\begin{bmatrix}\operatorname{ln}u \\ 5 \\ {u}^{2}\end{bmatrix}$ and $u(t)=\operatorname{ln}⁡t$, then  $(\mathbf{g}∘u)^{'}(t)=$
:question/worked-solution:
By the chain rule, we have 

$$
(\mathbf{f}∘u)^{'}(t)={\mathbf{f}}^{'}(u(t)){u}^{'}(t).
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{\mathbf{g}}^{'}(u) & =\begin{bmatrix}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}\operatorname{ln}u \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}\hspace{0.167em}\hspace{0.167em}5\hspace{0.167em}\hspace{0.167em} \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}\hspace{0.167em}\hspace{0.167em}{u}^{2}\hspace{0.167em}\hspace{0.167em}\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}\frac{1}{u} \\ 0 \\ 2u\end{bmatrix} \\ {u}^{'}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}t)=\frac{1}{t}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf{g}∘u)^{'}(t) & =\mathbf{g}'(u(t))u'(t) \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}\frac{1}{u(t)} \\ 0 \\ 2u(t)\end{bmatrix}{u}^{'}(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{t}\begin{bmatrix}\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}t} \\ 0 \\ 2\operatorname{ln}t\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}\frac{1}{t\operatorname{ln}t} \\ 0 \\ \frac{2\operatorname{ln}t}{t}\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

:question/problem:
Find $(\mathbf{f}\cdot \mathbf{g})^{'}(t)$, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf{f}(t) & =\operatorname{ln}t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+\frac{1}{t}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k} \\ \mathbf{g}(t) & =t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+\frac{1}{t}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+\operatorname{ln}t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k}\end{aligned}
$$
:question/worked-solution:
Using the dot product rule, we can write:

$$
(\mathbf{f}\cdot \mathbf{g})^{'}(t)={\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t)\cdot \mathbf{g}(t)+\mathbf{f}(t)\cdot {\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t)
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}t)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}\left(\frac{1}{t}\right)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k} \\  & =\frac{1}{t}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+\left(-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}\right)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+1\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k} \\  & =\frac{1}{t}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+\mathbf{k} \\ {\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}\left(\frac{1}{t}\right)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}t)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k} \\  & =1\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+\left(-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}\right)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+\frac{1}{t}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k} \\  & =\mathbf{i}-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+\frac{1}{t}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf{f}\cdot \mathbf{g})^{'}(t) & ={\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t)\cdot \mathbf{g}(t)+\mathbf{f}(t)\cdot {\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t) \\  & =(\frac{1}{t}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+\mathbf{k})\cdot (t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+\frac{1}{t}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+\operatorname{ln}t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k})+(\operatorname{ln}t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+\frac{1}{t}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k})\cdot (\mathbf{i}-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+\frac{1}{t}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k}) \\  & =(\frac{1}{t}\cdot t-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}\cdot \frac{1}{t}+1\cdot \operatorname{ln}t)+(\operatorname{ln}t\cdot 1+\frac{1}{t}\left(-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}\right)+t\cdot \frac{1}{t}) \\  & =1-\frac{1}{{t}^{3}}+\operatorname{ln}t+\operatorname{ln}t-\frac{1}{{t}^{3}}+1 \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}t+2-\frac{2}{{t}^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

:question/problem: Find $(v(t)\mathbf{f}(t))^{'}$ given that  $\mathbf{f}(t)=⟨{2}^{t},\hspace{0.222em}{2}^{t+1},\hspace{0.222em}{2}^{2t}+1⟩$ and $v(t)=\frac{1}{{2}^{t}}.$

$$

$$

$$

:question/problem:

$$

Let's find the derivatives of each function:

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf{f}(t)+4\mathbf{g}(t))^{'} & ={\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t)+4{\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t) \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}},\hspace{0.222em}\frac{1}{t},\hspace{0.222em}0⟩+4⟨1,\hspace{0.222em}-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\hspace{0.222em}4{t}^{3}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}},\hspace{0.222em}\frac{1}{t},\hspace{0.222em}0⟩+⟨4,\hspace{0.222em}-\frac{4}{{t}^{2}},\hspace{0.222em}16{t}^{3}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}+4,\hspace{0.222em}\frac{1}{t}-\frac{4}{{t}^{2}},\hspace{0.222em}0+16{t}^{3}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1+8\sqrt{t}}{2\sqrt{t}},\hspace{0.222em}\frac{t-4}{{t}^{2}},\hspace{0.222em}16{t}^{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

:question/problem: Find $(u(t)\mathbf{f}(t))^{'}$ where $\mathbf{f}(t)=\begin{bmatrix}t \\ {t}^{2} \\ {t}^{3}\end{bmatrix}$ and $u(t)=\operatorname{ln}⁡t.$
:question/worked-solution:
Using the scalar function multiple rule, we can write

$$
(u(t)\mathbf{f}(t))^{'}={u}^{'}(t)\mathbf{f}(t)+u(t){\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t)
$$

Let's find ${u}^{′}(t)$ and ${\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t).$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t) & =\begin{bmatrix}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3})\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2t \\ 3{t}^{2}\end{bmatrix} \\ {u}^{'}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}t)=\frac{1}{t}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(u(t)\mathbf{f}(t))^{'} & ={u}^{'}(t)\mathbf{f}(t)+u(t){\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{t}\begin{bmatrix}t \\ {t}^{2} \\ {t}^{3}\end{bmatrix}+\operatorname{ln}t\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2t \\ 3{t}^{2}\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ t \\ {t}^{2}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}\operatorname{ln}t \\ 2t\operatorname{ln}t \\ 3{t}^{2}\operatorname{ln}t\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}1+\operatorname{ln}t \\ t+2t\operatorname{ln}t \\ {t}^{2}+3{t}^{2}\operatorname{ln}t\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

$$

:question/problem: If $\mathbf{f}(u)=\begin{bmatrix}\operatorname{sin}u \\ \operatorname{cos}u \\ {e}^{u}\end{bmatrix}$ and $u(t)=4t-3,$ then $(\mathbf{f}∘u)^{'}(t)=$

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\mathbf{f}}^{'}(u) & =\begin{bmatrix}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}(\operatorname{sin}u) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}\hspace{0.167em}(\operatorname{cos}u) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}({e}^{u})\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}\operatorname{cos}u \\ -\operatorname{sin}u \\ {e}^{u}\end{bmatrix} \\ {u}^{'}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t-3)=4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$

:question/problem:
Differentiate $\mathbf{f}(t)+\mathbf{g}(t)$ with respect to $t$, given that

$$
:question/worked-solution:
By the sum rule, we have

$$
(\mathbf{f}(t)+\mathbf{g}(t))^{'}={\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t)+{\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t).
$$

Let's find the derivatives of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-2t),\hspace{0.167em}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\hspace{0.167em}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}((t-1)^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\hspace{0.167em}2t,\hspace{0.167em}2(t-1)⟩ \\ {\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t+1),\hspace{0.167em}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-2t),\hspace{0.167em}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\hspace{0.167em}-2,\hspace{0.167em}3{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf{f}(t)+\mathbf{g}(t))^{'} & ={\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t)+{\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t) \\  & =⟨-2,\hspace{0.167em}2t,\hspace{0.167em}2t-2⟩+⟨1,\hspace{0.167em}-2,\hspace{0.167em}3{t}^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\hspace{0.167em}2t-2,\hspace{0.167em}3{t}^{2}+2t-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

:question/problem:
Find the value of $(\mathbf{f}(t)-2\mathbf{g}(t))^{'}$ at $t=1,$ if 

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf{f}(t) & =⟨{t}^{2},\hspace{0.167em}\operatorname{ln}t,\hspace{0.167em}{e}^{t-1}⟩, \\ \mathbf{g}(t) & =⟨2\sqrt{t},\hspace{0.167em}{t}^{3},\hspace{0.167em}3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
:question/worked-solution:
First, notice that

$$
(\mathbf{f}(t)-2\mathbf{g}(t))^{'}={\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t)-2{\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t).
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\hspace{0.167em}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}t),\hspace{0.167em}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t-1})⟩ \\  & =⟨2t,\hspace{0.167em}\frac{1}{t},\hspace{0.167em}{e}^{t-1}⟩ \\ {\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\sqrt{t}),\hspace{0.167em}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}),\hspace{0.167em}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{\sqrt{t}},\hspace{0.167em}3{t}^{2},\hspace{0.167em}0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf{f}(1)-2\mathbf{g}(1))^{'} & ={\mathbf{f}}^{'}(1)-2{\mathbf{g}}^{'}(1) \\  & =⟨2(1),\hspace{0.167em}\frac{1}{1},\hspace{0.167em}{e}^{1-1}⟩-2⟨\frac{1}{\sqrt{1}},\hspace{0.167em}3(1)^{2},\hspace{0.167em}0⟩ \\  & =⟨2,1,1⟩-2⟨1,3,0⟩ \\  & =⟨2,1,1⟩-⟨2,6,0⟩ \\  & =⟨0,-5,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

:question/problem: Find ${(u(t)\mathbf{f}(t))}^{'}$ where $\mathbf{f}(t)=\begin{bmatrix}{e}^{t} \\ {t}^{3} \\ {e}^{2t}\end{bmatrix}$ and $u(t)={e}^{-t}.$

$$
{(u(t)\mathbf{f}(t))}^{'}={u}^{'}(t)\mathbf{f}(t)+u(t){\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t).
$$

Let's find ${u}^{′}(t)$ and ${\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t).$

$$

:question/problem: If $\mathbf{f}(u)=\operatorname{ln}u\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+{u}^{2}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+\sqrt{u}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k}$ and $u(t)={e}^{-t},$ then $(\mathbf{f}∘u)^{'}(t)=$

$$
(\mathbf{f}∘u)^{'}(t)={\mathbf{f}}^{'}(u(t)){u}^{'}(t).
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{\mathbf{f}}^{'}(u) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}(\operatorname{ln}u)\mathbf{i}+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}({u}^{2})\mathbf{j}+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}(\sqrt{u})\mathbf{k} \\  & =\frac{1}{u}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+2u\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k} \\ {u}^{'}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t})=-{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf{f}∘u)^{'}(t) & ={\mathbf{f}}^{'}(u(t))\cdot {u}^{'}(t) \\  & =(\frac{1}{u(t)}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+2u(t)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u(t)}}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k})\cdot {u}^{'}(t) \\  & =(\frac{1}{{e}^{-t}}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+2{e}^{-t}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+\frac{1}{2\sqrt{{e}^{-t}}}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k})\cdot (-{e}^{-t}) \\  & =({e}^{t}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+2{e}^{-t}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+\frac{1}{2}{e}^{t/2}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k})\cdot (-{e}^{-t}) \\  & =-\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}-2{e}^{-2t}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}-\frac{1}{2}{e}^{-t/2}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k}.\end{aligned}
$$

:question/problem: If $\mathbf{g}(u)=⟨\frac{1}{u},\hspace{0.167em}\operatorname{ln}(u+1),\hspace{0.167em}1⟩$ and $u(t)=\frac{1}{t}$, then $(\mathbf{g}∘u)^{'}(t)=$
:question/worked-solution:
By the chain rule, we have 

$$
(\mathbf{g}∘u)^{'}(t)=\mathbf{g}'(u(t))u'(t).
$$

Now, let's find the derivatives of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\mathbf{g}}^{'}(u) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}\left(\frac{1}{u}\right),\hspace{0.167em}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}(\operatorname{ln}(u+1)),\hspace{0.167em}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{{u}^{2}},\hspace{0.167em}\frac{1}{u+1},\hspace{0.167em}0⟩ \\ {u}^{'}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}\left(\frac{1}{t}\right)=-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}

$$

:question/problem:
Find $(\mathbf{f}\times \mathbf{g})^{'}(t)$ given that

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf{f}(t) & =⟨t,\hspace{0.167em}5,\hspace{0.167em}{t}^{4}⟩, \\ \mathbf{g}(t) & =⟨{t}^{2},\hspace{0.167em}{t}^{3},\hspace{0.167em}t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
:question/worked-solution:
Using the cross product rule, we can write:

$$
(\mathbf{f}\times \mathbf{g})^{'}(t)={\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t)\times \mathbf{g}(t)+\mathbf{f}(t)\times {\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t)
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\hspace{0.167em}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5),\hspace{0.167em}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\hspace{0.167em}0,\hspace{0.167em}4{t}^{3}⟩ \\ {\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\hspace{0.167em}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}),\hspace{0.167em}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2t,\hspace{0.167em}3{t}^{2},\hspace{0.167em}1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t)\times \mathbf{g}(t) & =\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ 1 & 0 & 4{t}^{3} \\ {t}^{2} & {t}^{3} & t\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}0 & 4{t}^{3} \\ {t}^{3} & t\end{vmatrix}\mathbf{i}-\begin{vmatrix}1 & 4{t}^{3} \\ {t}^{2} & t\end{vmatrix}\mathbf{j}+\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 \\ {t}^{2} & {t}^{3}\end{vmatrix}\mathbf{k} \\  & =⟨-4{t}^{6},\hspace{0.167em}4{t}^{5}-t,\hspace{0.167em}{t}^{3}⟩, \\ \mathbf{f}(t)\times {\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t) & =\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ t & 5 & {t}^{4} \\ 2t & 3{t}^{2} & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}5 & {t}^{4} \\ 3{t}^{2} & 1\end{vmatrix}\mathbf{i}-\begin{vmatrix}t & {t}^{4} \\ 2t & 1\end{vmatrix}\mathbf{j}+\begin{vmatrix}t & 5 \\ 2t & 3{t}^{2}\end{vmatrix}\mathbf{k} \\  & =⟨5-3{t}^{6},\hspace{0.167em}2{t}^{5}-t,\hspace{0.167em}3{t}^{3}-10t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf{f}\times \mathbf{g})^{'}(t) & =⟨-4{t}^{6},\hspace{0.167em}4{t}^{5}-t,\hspace{0.167em}{t}^{3}⟩+⟨5-3{t}^{6},\hspace{0.167em}2{t}^{5}-t,\hspace{0.167em}3{t}^{3}-10t⟩ \\  & =⟨-7{t}^{6}+5,\hspace{0.167em}6{t}^{5}-2t,\hspace{0.167em}4{t}^{3}-10t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

:question/problem:
Find $(\mathbf{f}\times \mathbf{g})^{'}(t)$ given that

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf{f}(t) & =⟨6{t}^{2},\hspace{0.222em}2t,\hspace{0.222em}6⟩ \\ \mathbf{g}(t) & =⟨3,\hspace{0.222em}3{t}^{2},\hspace{0.222em}4t-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$
:question/worked-solution:
Using the cross product rule, we can write:

$$
(\mathbf{f}\times \mathbf{g})^{'}(t)={\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t)\times \mathbf{g}(t)+\mathbf{f}(t)\times {\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t)
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6{t}^{2}),\hspace{0.222em}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\hspace{0.222em}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6)⟩ \\  & =⟨12t,\hspace{0.222em}2,\hspace{0.222em}0⟩ \\ {\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3),\hspace{0.222em}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}),\hspace{0.222em}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t-1)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\hspace{0.222em}6t,\hspace{0.222em}4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t)\times \mathbf{g}(t) & =\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ 12t & 2 & 0 \\ 3 & 3{t}^{2} & (4t-1)\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}2 & 0 \\ 3{t}^{2} & (4t-1)\end{vmatrix}\mathbf{i}-\begin{vmatrix}12t & 0 \\ 3 & (4t-1)\end{vmatrix}\mathbf{j}+\begin{vmatrix}12t & 2 \\ 3 & 3{t}^{2}\end{vmatrix}\mathbf{k} \\  & =⟨8t-2,\hspace{0.222em}12t-48{t}^{2},\hspace{0.222em}36{t}^{3}-6⟩ \\ \mathbf{f}(t)\times {\mathbf{g}}^{'}(t) & =\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ 6{t}^{2} & 2t & 6 \\ 0 & 6t & 4\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}2t & 6 \\ 6t & 4\end{vmatrix}\mathbf{i}-\begin{vmatrix}6{t}^{2} & 6 \\ 0 & 4\end{vmatrix}\mathbf{j}+\begin{vmatrix}6{t}^{2} & 2t \\ 0 & 6t\end{vmatrix}\mathbf{k} \\  & =⟨-28t,\hspace{0.222em}-24{t}^{2},\hspace{0.222em}36{t}^{3}⟩\end{aligned}

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf{f}\times \mathbf{g})^{'}(t) & =⟨8t-2,\hspace{0.222em}12t-48{t}^{2},\hspace{0.222em}36{t}^{3}-6⟩+⟨-28t,\hspace{0.222em}-24{t}^{2},\hspace{0.222em}36{t}^{3}⟩ \\  & =⟨-20t-2,\hspace{0.222em}-72{t}^{2}+12t,\hspace{0.222em}72{t}^{3}-6⟩\end{aligned}

:question/problem: Given $\mathbf{f}(t)=⟨1-{t}^{2}\hspace{0.167em},\hspace{0.167em}1-{t}^{3}\hspace{0.167em},\hspace{0.167em}1-t⟩$, find $({\mathbf{f}}^{'}\times \mathbf{f})^{'}(t).$
:question/worked-solution:
Using the cross product rule, we can write:

$$({\mathbf{f}}^{'}\times \mathbf{f})^{'}(t)={\mathbf{f}}^{''}(t)\times \mathbf{f}(t)+{\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t)\times {\mathbf{f}}^{'}(t)$$

Let's now find the first and second derivative of the function.

$$

$$

Calculate the first product-rule term and the second product-rule term, denoted $P_1$ and $P_2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}P_1 & =(0)(-1)+(6)(3)+(2)(0) \\  & =18 \\ P_2 & =(0)(0)+(0)(0)+(0)(0) \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Add the two terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}(f^{\prime}\cdot f)^{\prime}(0) & =P_1+P_2 \\  & =18\end{aligned}
$$

:question/problem:
Find $(f\cdot g)^{\prime}(t)$ given that

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =(t - 2)\,i- 2 t\,j+t\,k \\ g(t) & =(t^{2} + t)\,i+t\,j+t^{3}\,k\end{aligned}
$$
:question/worked-solution:
Use the dot product rule, preserving the factor order:

$$
(f\cdot g)^{\prime}(t)=f^{\prime}(t)\cdot g(t)+f(t)\cdot g^{\prime}(t)
$$

Differentiate each component:

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{\prime}_{1}(t) & =\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(t - 2)=1 \\ f^{\prime}_{2}(t) & =\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(- 2 t)=-2 \\ f^{\prime}_{3}(t) & =\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(t)=1 \\ f^{\prime}(t) & =\,i-2\,j+\,k \\ g^{\prime}_{1}(t) & =\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(t^{2} + t)=2 t + 1 \\ g^{\prime}_{2}(t) & =\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(t)=1 \\ g^{\prime}_{3}(t) & =\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(t^{3})=3 t^{2} \\ g^{\prime}(t) & =(2 t + 1)\,i+\,j+3 t^{2}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate the first product-rule term and the second product-rule term, denoted $P_1$ and $P_2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}P_1 & =(1)(t^{2} + t)+(-2)(t)+(1)(t^{3}) \\  & =t^{3} + t^{2} - t \\ P_2 & =(t - 2)(2 t + 1)+(- 2 t)(1)+(t)(3 t^{2}) \\  & =3 t^{3} + 2 t^{2} - 5 t - 2\end{aligned}
$$

Add the two terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}(f\cdot g)^{\prime}(t) & =P_1+P_2 \\  & =4 t^{3} + 3 t^{2} - 6 t - 2\end{aligned}
$$

:question/problem:
Find $(f\cdot g)^{\prime}(t)$ given that

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =- 3 \ln{(t )}\,i- 2 t\,j+\frac{2}{t}\,k \\ g(t) & =- 3 t\,i+3 \ln{(t )}\,j- \frac{2}{t}\,k\end{aligned}
$$ Assume $t>0$.
:question/worked-solution:
Use the dot product rule, preserving the factor order:

$$
(f\cdot g)^{\prime}(t)=f^{\prime}(t)\cdot g(t)+f(t)\cdot g^{\prime}(t)
$$

Differentiate each component:

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{\prime}_{1}(t) & =\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(- 3 \ln{(t )})=- \frac{3}{t} \\ f^{\prime}_{2}(t) & =\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(- 2 t)=-2 \\ f^{\prime}_{3}(t) & =\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\left(\frac{2}{t}\right)=- \frac{2}{t^{2}} \\ f^{\prime}(t) & =- \frac{3}{t}\,i-2\,j- \frac{2}{t^{2}}\,k \\ g^{\prime}_{1}(t) & =\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(- 3 t)=-3 \\ g^{\prime}_{2}(t) & =\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(3 \ln{(t )})=\frac{3}{t} \\ g^{\prime}_{3}(t) & =\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\left(- \frac{2}{t}\right)=\frac{2}{t^{2}} \\ g^{\prime}(t) & =-3\,i+\frac{3}{t}\,j+\frac{2}{t^{2}}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate the first product-rule term and the second product-rule term, denoted $P_1$ and $P_2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}P_1 & =\left(- \frac{3}{t}\right)(- 3 t)+(-2)(3 \ln{(t )})+\left(- \frac{2}{t^{2}}\right)\left(- \frac{2}{t}\right) \\  & =- 6 \ln{(t )} + 9 + \frac{4}{t^{3}} \\ P_2 & =(- 3 \ln{(t )})(-3)+(- 2 t)\left(\frac{3}{t}\right)+\left(\frac{2}{t}\right)\left(\frac{2}{t^{2}}\right) \\  & =9 \ln{(t )} - 6 + \frac{4}{t^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Add the two terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}(f\cdot g)^{\prime}(t) & =P_1+P_2 \\  & =3 \ln{(t )} + 3 + \frac{8}{t^{3}}\end{aligned}

:question/problem: Given $f(t)=⟨3 t^{3} + 3,\,2 t,\,2 t^{2} + 1⟩$, find $(f^{\prime}\cdot f)^{\prime}(t).$

Use the dot product rule, preserving the factor order:

$$
(f^{\prime}\cdot f)^{\prime}(t)=f^{\prime\prime}(t)\cdot f(t)+f^{\prime}(t)\cdot f^{\prime}(t)
$$

Differentiate each component:

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{\prime}_{1}(t) & =\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(3 t^{3} + 3)=9 t^{2} \\ f^{\prime}_{2}(t) & =\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(2 t)=2 \\ f^{\prime}_{3}(t) & =\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(2 t^{2} + 1)=4 t \\ f^{\prime}(t) & =⟨9 t^{2},\,2,\,4 t⟩ \\ f^{\prime\prime}_{1}(t) & =\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(9 t^{2})=18 t \\ f^{\prime\prime}_{2}(t) & =\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(2)=0 \\ f^{\prime\prime}_{3}(t) & =\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(4 t)=4 \\ f^{\prime\prime}(t) & =⟨18 t,\,0,\,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate the first product-rule term and the second product-rule term, denoted $P_1$ and $P_2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}P_1 & =(18 t)(3 t^{3} + 3)+(0)(2 t)+(4)(2 t^{2} + 1) \\  & =54 t^{4} + 8 t^{2} + 54 t + 4 \\ P_2 & =(9 t^{2})(9 t^{2})+(2)(2)+(4 t)(4 t) \\  & =81 t^{4} + 16 t^{2} + 4\end{aligned}
$$

Add the two terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}(f^{\prime}\cdot f)^{\prime}(t) & =P_1+P_2 \\  & =135 t^{4} + 24 t^{2} + 54 t + 8\end{aligned}
$$

:question/problem: Given $f(t)=- 3 t^{3}\,i+(3 t^{2} - 2)\,j+2 t\,k$, find $(f^{\prime}\cdot f)^{\prime}(t).$

$$
(f^{\prime}\cdot f)^{\prime}(t)=f^{\prime\prime}(t)\cdot f(t)+f^{\prime}(t)\cdot f^{\prime}(t)
$$

Differentiate each component:

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{\prime}_{1}(t) & =\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(- 3 t^{3})=- 9 t^{2} \\ f^{\prime}_{2}(t) & =\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(3 t^{2} - 2)=6 t \\ f^{\prime}_{3}(t) & =\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(2 t)=2 \\ f^{\prime}(t) & =- 9 t^{2}\,i+6 t\,j+2\,k \\ f^{\prime\prime}_{1}(t) & =\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(- 9 t^{2})=- 18 t \\ f^{\prime\prime}_{2}(t) & =\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(6 t)=6 \\ f^{\prime\prime}_{3}(t) & =\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(2)=0 \\ f^{\prime\prime}(t) & =- 18 t\,i+6\,j\end{aligned}

Calculate the first product-rule term and the second product-rule term, denoted $P_1$ and $P_2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}P_1 & =(- 18 t)(- 3 t^{3})+(6)(3 t^{2} - 2)+(0)(2 t) \\  & =54 t^{4} + 18 t^{2} - 12 \\ P_2 & =(- 9 t^{2})(- 9 t^{2})+(6 t)(6 t)+(2)(2) \\  & =81 t^{4} + 36 t^{2} + 4\end{aligned}
